title: Pinakothek der Moderne exhibition explores how art interacts with space
summary: The spaces we inhabit shape our perception, our sense of place, and the ways we move through them. As viewers, therefore, we never experience art divorced from the surrounding space. Under the title Between & Beyond, the Sammlung Moderne Kunst at the Pinakothek der Moderne presents works from its own collection that explore both the aesthetic and social perception of the gallery space. On display are paintings, objects, and installations from the 1960s to the present day, examining the fluid relationship between the artwork, the space, and the viewer. In the 1960s, artists associated with Minimal Art began incorporating the surrounding space into their works. The result was installations that engaged viewers in a physical and sensory experience and could only be fully appreciated in situ. title: The McNay to present the poetic world of celebrated South Korean artist Suki Seokyeong Kang
summary: The McNay Art Museum will present “Suki Seokyeong Kang: Mountain—Hour—Face,” the first solo exhibition by a South Korean artist in the museum's history, from Oct. 30, 2026-Jan. 24, 2027. Featuring nearly 40 works created between 2014 and 2024, the exhibition brings together sculpture, painting, textiles, installation, video and poetry in a sweeping look at Kang's multidisciplinary practice. Organized by the Museum of Contemporary Art Denver and adapted for the McNay by Lauren Thompson, curator of exhibitions at the McNay Art Museum, “Mountain—Hour—Face” transforms the galleries into an immersive environment shaped by rhythm, abstraction and the natural world. title: High Museum of Art presents works on paper exhibition centered on tree studies
summary: This summer, the High Museum of Art opened “Paper Trees” (July 31, 2026-Feb. 21, 2027), an exhibition that ponders the role and presence of trees in American art from the 19th century to the present. Featuring nearly 50 prints, drawings and sculptures from the High’s collection as well as loans from the Robert C. Williams Museum of Papermaking and Clark Atlanta University Art Museum, the exhibition traces different schools of thought in the depiction and representation of landscape and the natural world. “By bringing these works together, we invite audiences to consider how artists have helped inspire reverence for nature, using the tree as a beautiful symbol of life,” said Rand Suffolk, director of the High. title: The Rollins Museum of Art unveils reinstallation of its permanent collection of contemporary art at The Alfond Inn
summary: The Rollins Museum of Art announces the annual reinstallation of its Alfond Collection of Contemporary art at The Alfond Inn, introducing newly acquired artwork and first-time installations that reflect the Museum's continued commitment to building a globally significant collection. As the only hotel in the United States designed as a living extension of an art museum, The Alfond Inn offers guests a unique opportunity to experience artwork by internationally renowned artists throughout its public spaces. Curated by the Rollins Museum of Art, these dynamic installations transform the philanthropic boutique hotel into an accessible cultural destination where visitors can engage with contemporary art every day of the year. title: TAI Modern presents second solo exhibition by Japanese bamboo artist Kawano Shoko
summary: TAI Modern is presenting Kawano Shoko, the gallery's second solo exhibition of work by Japanese bamboo artist Kawano Shoko, on view from July 31 through August 22. This exhibition arrives ten years after the artists first show at TAI Modern and follows upon his being awarded Japan’s Medal with Purple Ribbon in 2024. Constructed from finely prepared bamboo strips, woven with the artist’s signature sukashi-ajiro (open twill plaiting), Kawano's works emphasize organic form, openness, and the natural flexibility of bamboo. Space and rhythm are integral to each composition. Kawano frequently adds an exterior layer of carved, parallel bamboo plates to an open twill-plaited form, based on a technique learned from Hayakawa Shōkōsai V during the Living National Treasure workshops he led in 2006–07. title: Baltimore Museum of Art elects Elizabeth J. Himelfarb Hurwitz as Board Chair
summary: The Baltimore Museum of Art Board of Trustees has elected Elizabeth J. Himelfarb Hurwitz as its next Board Chair. She succeeds James D. Thornton, who served as Chair since 2022. A Baltimore native, interior designer, and dedicated arts supporter, Hurwitz has served in several leadership and volunteer roles at the BMA for more than a decade, helping to shape the institution’s strategic vision, strengthen audience engagement, and advance its commitment to building meaningful connections through art. Since joining the BMA Board of Trustees in 2020, Hurwitz has taken on key leadership roles across the institution. Most recently, she led the museum’s 2026 strategic planning initiative that encapsulates the vision for the BMA’s future. title: Immersive ceramic artist Maura Wright brings decorative arts inspiration to Cheekwood residency
summary: Nationally recognized artist Maura Wright, known for creating immersive installations that blend sculptural ceramics and historic ornament, has been selected as Cheekwood Estate & Gardens' 2026 Martin Shallenberger Artist-in-Residence. Wright's practice centers on intricately crafted clay vessels and sculptural forms. Working primarily in earthenware, she draws inspiration from decorative arts history, domestic objects, and folk traditions. Her installations combine richly ornamented ceramics with painted environments that evoke frescoed interiors and decorative wall treatments, exploring the relationship between objects and the spaces they inhabit. During her residency, Wright will draw inspiration from Cheekwood's decorative arts collections, Historic Mansion, and expansive gardens. title: Ogden Contemporary Arts announces Zachary Fabri as 2026 Artist in Residence
summary: Ogden Contemporary Arts announced Zachary Fabri as its 2026 Artist in Residence. Fabri, a Brooklyn-based interdisciplinary artist working in lens-based media and public space, will be in residence at OCA from August 1 through October 4, 2026, developing a new body of work inspired by the landscape, history, and the communities of northern Utah. The residency will result in a solo exhibition opening with a live performance on Friday, October 2, 2026. During his residency, Fabri will investigate the history and presence of salt extraction in Utah, asking two deceptively simple questions: What is taken? What remains? Working across video, photography, sculpture, and drawing, he will trace how these questions reverberate from the extractive labor practices of the trans-Atlantic slave trade into Black culture today. title: Beyond the postcard: David Saxe reveals a more intimate Cuba in 'Cuba es Vida'
summary: Cuba has long inspired photographers with its vibrant streets, colorful architecture, and unmistakable atmosphere. In Cuba es Vida, David Saxe looks beyond these familiar images to reveal a more personal and nuanced portrait of the island. Created over the course of three journeys, the project explores the rhythms of everyday life, where history, resilience, and human connection quietly unfold. Rather than documenting Cuba's iconic landmarks, Saxe is drawn to its people and the moments that often go unnoticed. Musicians rehearsing in empty theaters, fishermen preparing their boats at dawn, children training in boxing gyms and ballet schools, and elderly residents reflecting on lives shaped by history become the heart of the story. His photographs celebrate ordinary life while revealing the remarkable spirit that continues to define the country. What distinguishes Cuba es Vida is its visual language. title: PICA announces 2026 Dr Harold Schenberg Arts Awards recipients
summary: Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts (PICA) has announced the recipients of this year’s Dr Harold Schenberg Arts Awards at the opening night of the Hatched: National Graduate Show 2026, recognising emerging artists from across Australia through a $50,000 prize pool, the country’s largest dedicated to supporting artists at a pivotal stage in their practice. The following three recipients will each receive a $15,000 award for their exceptional works as part of the 2026 Dr Harold Schenberg Arts Awards: • Lychandra Anastasia Gieseman, University of Tasmania (TAS), for Rev(olution)s / To Loves Ruin, 2025. • Tabitha Glanville, Monash University (VIC), for gyrr ngaya bina-guwal winangaylahna (I am listening now with different ears), 2025. • Jessica Shannon, North Metropolitan TAFE (WA), for Allowing the Dust to Settle and In-Tension, 2025.

title: Before 'SNL' and 'SCTV': New doc traces the birth of modern comedy
summary: Film Forum will present the U.S. theatrical premiere of Nick Davis’ You Had to Be There: How the Toronto Godspell Ignited the Comedy Revolution, Spread Love & Overalls, and Created a Community that Changed the World (in a Canadian Kind of Way) on Friday, September 18. The 1972 Toronto production of the musical Godspell featured an eye-popping cast of future comedy titans: Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Andrea Martin, Gilda Radner, Dave Thomas — with Victor Garber as a hippie Jesus and Paul Shaffer as musical director. The production itself was supposed to play for only a handful of weeks, but was such a smash hit that it was extended and ran for over a year and a half, during which time Martin and Levy became original members of Second City Television, and Garber left to star in the feature film of Godspell. title: RM Sotheby's announces largest auction in company history for Monterey Car Week
summary: RM Sotheby’s returns to California’s Monterey Peninsula for its 29th consecutive year with the largest and most valuable auction in company history. The 199-lot offering brings together 120 years of automotive history, from pioneering coachbuilt masterpieces and legendary competition cars to the world’s most coveted modern hypercars. Led by the historic 1996 McLaren F1 GTR “The Pop Art F1,” the celebrated 1962 Aston Martin DB4 GT Zagato, the legendary 1963 Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport, and an exceptional group of Ferrari halo cars, Monterey once again demonstrates the depth, quality and global reach that have defined RM Sotheby’s flagship sale for nearly three decades. 1996 McLaren F1 GTR “The Pop Art F1” - The first 1996-specification F1 GTR and one of two factory “XP” Short-Tail prototypes, chassis 10R is the only example finished in McLaren’s scarlet-and-yellow “Pop Art” livery. title: Benaki Museum opens Aleksandra Waliszewska exhibition in Athens
summary: The Adam Mickiewicz Institute announced the exhibition Aleksandra Waliszewska: Irruption of Antiquity, organized by the DESTE Foundation in collaboration with the Benaki Museum and curated by Alison M. Gingeras. The exhibition opened on June 3, 2026, at the Benaki Museum of Greek Culture in Athens and will run through September 27, 2026. Spanning two floors of the museum, the exhibition features sixteen paintings by Polish artist Aleksandra Waliszewska placed in charged iconographic tension with objects from Neolithic Greece, classical antiquity, the Byzantine world, and the modern Greek era. The exhibition pays homage to Greece as the birthplace of figurative and narrative art while tracing the enduring presence of antiquity within the contemporary visual imagination. title: Leighton House's The Arab Hall: Past and Present presents video art commission by Soraya Syed
summary: Leighton House presents From Water, Every Living Thing, a new site-specific video installation by London-born artist Soraya Syed, as part of the museum’s interdisciplinary project The Arab Hall: Past and Present. On display from 30 July to 4 October 2026, this new commission transforms the Hall's historic fountain into a living work where moving calligraphy, projection, water and sound come together in dialogue with one of Britain's most extraordinary interiors. title: Frick announces expansion of fellowship program
summary: The Frick Collection, long known for its prestigious art historical fellowships, announces the growth of these offerings through the creation of six new positions, underwritten by a series of major gifts. Alongside the ongoing Anne L. Poulet Curatorial Fellowship, now in its third decade, the Frick hosts new curatorial, conservation, and music-related roles, supporting many of the museum’s activities while expanding access to career-shaping experiences for rising arts and culture professionals. The six new positions, created since 2024, are the Ayesha Bulchandani Music Fellowship, the Alexis Gregory Fellowship for European Decorative Arts, The Eric & Jane Nord Family Fund Conservation and Curatorial Fellowships, the Louis Vuitton Curatorial Research Associate, and the Stephen K. and Janie Woo Scher Fellowship. title: The Portland Art Museum transforms South Park Blocks with monumental asphalt artwork
summary: The Portland Art Museum will celebrate the opening of the new Cultural District Plaza in downtown Portland with a community free day on Saturday, August 8. The centerpiece of the new pedestrian plaza is a monumental asphalt painting, Mountains Full of Blessings, designed by multi-disciplinary British-Nigerian artist & designer Yinka Ilori, MBE, and painted by hundreds of volunteers at a community painting day in July. The August 8 Miller Family Free Day opening celebration will feature a ribbon cutting at noon, followed by an artist talk with Ilori, a site-responsive performance by Heidi Duckler Dance/Northwest and 45th Parallel Universe, and free admission to the Museum from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. The new pedestrian plaza on Southwest Madison Street marks the crowning milestone of the city’s major downtown cultural expansion. title: Carried by rivers, held by lands at Remai Modern
summary: Remai Modern’s ambitious multi-year project Carried by rivers, held by lands continues through the remainder of 2026 with a group exhibition, installation and gathering that showcase a set of artist projects developed during exchanges, gatherings, and site-responsive processes over the last three years. Featuring Cooking Sections, Kultivator, Katarina Pirak Sikku, Katarina Spik Skum, Althea Thauberger, Marianne Nicolson with Dzawada̱ʼenux̱w First Nation community members, and Laakkuluk Wiliamson and Jamie Griffiths, the works in the project’s eponymous exhibition attend to the flows that sustain and unsettle life—ecological, cultural, and economic. title: Open call: 15th Muslim Mulliqi International Exhibition at National Gallery of Kosova
summary: The National Gallery of Kosova announced the open call for the 15th edition of Muslim Mulliqi International Exhibition, titled RADICAL COPIES, curated by May Makki. In 1979, the Prizren-born conceptual artist Goran Đorđević launched an international strike of the “art system.” Denouncing what he described as the artist's alienation from the conditions and products of artistic labor, he called on fellow artists—such as Marina Abramović, Hans Haacke, Lucy Lippard, and Sol LeWitt—to boycott the system for several months. Forty artists responded, and while some expressed curiosity or enthusiasm, most declined. title: Edinburgh Art Festival presents 2026 edition
summary: EAF26 presents alternative perspectives across the breadth of the city. At EAF’s new permanent space at 92 Constitution Street, Love Bites Back is an exhibition of work by Del LaGrace Volcano drawn from their Queer Archive of Resistance, focusing on photographs made in the UK, including Edinburgh, between 1980s and 90s. Emerging from lived involvement in leather dyke culture, embodied politics and queer identity, these images challenge normative ideas of gender, desire, and power. A sister show at Auto Italia in London, Sensual / Mutual, returns to the early 1980s and to the queer subcultural spaces that both sheltered and shaped Volcano’s Practice. title: Exhibition of recent work by Richard Tuttle opens at Dia Beacon
summary: Dia Art Foundation opened Richard Tuttle: Half-Light at Dia Beacon. Bringing Richard Tuttle’s work to Dia’s galleries for the first time, this exhibition features two recent series by the artist—one of which recently entered Dia’s permanent collection, the other realized onsite in response to it. Presenting distinct methods of making and installation, these series extend Tuttle’s lifelong investigation into systems of meaning andreality. Richard Tuttle: Half-Light opened July 31, 2026, and will be on long-term view. “Richard Tuttle is deeply engaged with light, scale, seriality, and space—areas of exploration that are paramount to Dia’s legacy.
